facts.text: Morningside Heights hosts a dense cluster of higher‑education campuses, including Columbia, Barnard, Teachers College, Union Theological Seminary, and Jewish Theological Seminary.
Low Memorial Library on Columbia’s campus is a National Historic Landmark and city‑designated interior and exterior landmark.
Riverside Church, between 120th and 122nd Streets, is both a city landmark and NRHP site, sharing the space with Grant’s Tomb.
The 125th Street subway station and its viaduct over the valley are designated New York City landmarks and listed on the NRHP.
In 1968, protests erupted over Columbia’s plan to build a gym in Morningside Park, highlighting racial tensions between the university and Harlem.
The Plant and Scrymser pavilions at Mount Sinai Morningside, built in the early 20th century, are recognized as city landmarks and NRHP sites.
